title: Sports Card Grading Near Me (2026)
verdict: Sports card grading near me is easiest through AGS in 2026: mail-in from anywhere, drop-off at select locations, $18 a card.

Almost no grading company grades in your town. PSA, CGC, Beckett and SGC all work by mail from a few labs, and appear in person mainly at large card shows. The practical choice is between mailing cards yourself, paying a shop to do it, or using a grader that takes drop-offs.

list: Mail them to a grader yourself. This is how most sports cards are graded. AGS returns standard orders in 20 business days or less.
Use a card shop. The shop ships your sports cards to a grading company and adds a handling fee. Ask which grader, which tier and the full price.
Drop them off. AGS accepts in-person drop-offs at select locations, including secure intake at its headquarters at 727 Page Ave, Staten Island, New York. Confirm with AGS first.
Go to a card show. Large shows often have graders accepting submissions, and some grade on site at premium prices.

why: AGS is one of the few graders you can hand sports cards to. It accepts drop-offs at select AGS locations, including secure intake at its Staten Island headquarters, and its scanner is compact enough to grade on site. Message AGS before you travel to confirm where intake is open.

Human grading is a judgment made in seconds, and it varies. AGS replaces the judgment with a measurement: a 3D laser maps the card, software scores centering, corners, edges and surface, and the grade follows from the numbers. That is why AGS says a regrade rarely moves.
The process is short. You enter the cards online, ship them in sleeves and semi-rigid holders, and follow the order in your dashboard. AGS also takes drop-offs at select locations.

faq.q: Is there sports card grading near me?
faq.a: There is rarely a grader in town. You can mail sports cards to a grader, drop them at a select AGS location, hand them to a card shop that forwards them for a fee, or find a grader at a card show.

faq.q: What costs come on top of the grading fee?
faq.a: Shipping to the grader, return shipping and insurance, and supplies such as penny sleeves and card savers. Some graders add membership fees, subgrade fees or value upcharges. AGS adds return shipping at checkout.
Rarely. Many act as middlemen: they collect cards, batch them, send them to a grading company and add a handling fee. Ask which grader they use, which tier, and what the total will be.

faq.q: Can I get cards graded at a card show?
faq.a: Sometimes. Large graders take submissions at big shows, and a few grade on site at premium prices. AGS's scanner is compact enough for on-site grading. Check the show's exhibitor list and each grader's schedule.

faq.q: Is mailing cards for grading safe?
faq.a: Yes, if you pack them properly and use a tracked, insured service. AGS returns cards with tracking and offers optional insurance on the return shipment.
